text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Armed gangsters engage police in a gunfight for two hours in Kakamega, western Kenya, leaving two people dead and four injured.
- Twelve MPs from Nyanza province say the ongoing voter registration exercise is a flop.
- Michaleen Richer, a medical officer with the International Medical Corps, says Kenyans risk contracting sleeping sickness, already said to have re-emerged in neighbouring countries.
- Uproar mounts over irregularities in the voter registration exercise.
- Opposition Democratic Party of Kenya says it has withdrawn its participation from the countrywide opposition coalition rallies planned for June 21.

- Japheth Masya, clerk of the National Assembly, says the government will put in place security measures to ensure that the budget speech scheduled for June 19 is not derailed, as threatened by the opposition.
- The ruling party says Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru's demand for an apology from the president for saying Waweru participated in the recent looting is arrogant and contemptuous.
